Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- CNN wants to hear from viewers in both English and Russian for its weeklong focus on modern Russia. CNN Moscow Correspondent at Star City, the Russian cosmonaut training facility. Reflecting on Dmitry Medvedev's first year as president, and looking ahead to President Obama's first trip to the Kremlin in July, CNN delves beyond politics to profile the many facets of this vast land through an ambitious bi-lingual audience initiative and a wide-ranging week of programming. The audience initiative -- CNN's first with a Russian-language component -- complements an energetic mix of live reporting and interviews, feature and documentary programming, and cultural despatches running the gamut of sports to space travel, fashion to music, business to farming, as CNN travels the length of the country to bring viewers the Russia of today. CNN wants to hear from both Russian residents and worldwide viewers, in English or in Russian, what they think about Russia's role in the international community. Send us your comments via Sound Off below. or send your videos and pictures via iReport or to youtube.com/CNN. The best will be posted online to be read and watched by CNN.com Youtube audiences around the world, while English language contributions have the additional opportunity to feature on air in CNN's programming output. "Russia is making its voice heard far beyond its borders at a time when the global community has never been more interdependent," said Mike McCarthy, CNN International's vice president of coverage and feature programming. "We want our compelling interviews and reports to stand alongside the very best in audience commentary to provide a really lively insight into what contemporary Russia looks like at a time when its impact is being felt not just in politics but in a diverse array of other fields. We're also excited to offer an online outlet for the first time for Russian language audience feedback as well." The week of programming kicks off with a special travelogue documentary Eye on Russia: Moving Forward where CNN's Moscow-based Senior International Correspondent Matthew Chance rides the train from the Arctic north of Murmansk down to the southern climes of Sochi by way of St Petersburg and Moscow, to offer a diverse range of reports. He visits a Russian farm to look at the country's ambitions to be an agricultural superpower, checks out the Star City astronaut training center, meets with seven-foot boxing world champion-turned-movie star Nikolai Valuev and talks along the way with entrepreneurs and environmentalists working to make the city of Sochi home to green Olympics in 2014. CNN also catches up with famous faces like NHL hockey star Alexander Ovechkin, Russian Vogue editor in chief Aliona Doletskaya, A list model Natalia Vodianova, acclaimed conductor Valery Gergiev, the "Russian Madonna" singer Valeriya, and London-based Russian art collector Nonna Materkova to bring together an eclectic mix of Russians who have made it on the world stage. Additionally, there are reports on Russian communities around the world that have sprung up in places as different as Ashdod, Israel and Brighton Beach, New York. CNN is also live every night from a range of iconic Moscow locations as Chance gives his topical insights into a country increasingly at the center of international headlines, to complement a range of interviews with top Russian CEOs and industry leaders airing throughout CNN's prime time evening programming. From St Basil's Cathedral, the Kremlin, Christ the Saviour Cathedral and Manej Square, Chance gives us the latest on what makes the Russia of today, from domestic and foreign policy, to business, to culture. The Eye on series has travelled around the world visiting France, Russia, India, South Korea, China, South Africa, Brazil, Beirut and Poland.

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**

# CNN Announces Weeklong Bilingual “Eye on Russia” Programming Initiative

### Special coverage will examine modern Russia through reporting, analysis and audience perspectives submitted in English and Russian

**ATLANTA, LONDON and HONG KONG —** CNN today announced **“Eye on Russia,”** a weeklong, multiplatform programming initiative offering an in-depth look at contemporary Russian society, politics, culture, business and daily life.

Running **Monday through Sunday** across CNN’s television, digital, social and streaming platforms, the special coverage will feature reporting from CNN correspondents, interviews with regional experts and voices from communities in Russia and around the world.

Programming will explore topics including Russia’s changing economy, technology and innovation, arts and culture, generational attitudes, regional identities, international relations and the experiences of Russians living at home and abroad. Selected reports and digital features will be available in both English and Russian.

“‘Eye on Russia’ is designed to move beyond headlines and give audiences a broader, more nuanced view of modern Russia,” a CNN spokesperson said. “By combining independent journalism with carefully verified audience contributions, we aim to reflect a wide range of experiences and perspectives.”

## Audience submissions

CNN is inviting audiences to participate by submitting short written accounts, photographs or videos responding to the question:

**English:** *What should the world understand about life in modern Russia?*  
**Русский:** *Что миру следует знать о жизни в современной России?*

Submissions may be made in **English or Russian** through CNN’s “Eye on Russia” online portal. Contributors should include their first name, general location and a brief description of their submission. Selected contributions may be translated and featured across CNN platforms.

All submissions will be reviewed in accordance with CNN’s editorial, verification, safety and privacy standards. Contributors should avoid sharing sensitive personal information or material that could place themselves or others at risk. Submission does not guarantee publication.

A complete programming schedule, submission guidelines and selected bilingual coverage will be available at **CNN.com/EyeOnRussia**.

**Русская версия и правила участия доступны на странице CNN.com/EyeOnRussia.**

### About CNN

CNN is a global news organization delivering breaking news, in-depth reporting and analysis across television, digital, streaming and social platforms worldwide.

**Media contact:**  
CNN Communications  
press@cnn.com

# CNN International Plans Wide-Ranging Russia Special Ahead of Obama’s Kremlin Visit

**Network to examine the country’s politics, economy, culture, sports and travel as Washington and Moscow seek to reset relations**

**LONDON —** CNN International is preparing a broad package of reports on contemporary Russia ahead of U.S. President Barack Obama’s July 2009 visit to Moscow, offering viewers a portrait of a country balancing renewed global influence with economic uncertainty and rapid social change.

The special coverage will move beyond the diplomatic agenda surrounding Obama’s trip to examine daily life, business, culture, sports and travel across Russia. Reports are expected to air throughout CNN International’s news and feature programming, supported by online stories, video and background material.

Obama is due to visit Moscow on July 6–8 for meetings with President Dmitry Medvedev and Prime Minister Vladimir Putin. The summit comes as both governments speak of “resetting” relations after years of disputes over NATO expansion, missile defense, the war in Georgia, energy security and Iran’s nuclear program.

Arms control is likely to dominate the official talks. Washington and Moscow are working toward a successor to the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty, or START, which expires in December. The two sides are also expected to discuss cooperation in Afghanistan, including transit routes for U.S. personnel and supplies, as well as wider nuclear nonproliferation efforts.

CNN International’s political reporting will examine the unusual power arrangement at the center of the Russian state. Medvedev became president in 2008, but Putin—his predecessor and the country’s dominant political figure for much of the decade—continues to wield substantial influence as prime minister.

Correspondents will assess whether Medvedev’s language about modernization, legal reform and the rule of law represents a significant shift or operates within the political system built during Putin’s presidency. The coverage will also consider the strength of opposition parties, the role of state television, restrictions facing independent media and the Kremlin’s relationship with Russia’s business elite.

Beyond Moscow’s corridors of power, the series will explore how Russians view their country’s place in the world. Nearly two decades after the collapse of the Soviet Union, Russia has regained confidence on the international stage, aided by energy revenues and a more assertive foreign policy. Yet its relationship with the West remains marked by suspicion on both sides.

## Economy under pressure

CNN’s business coverage will focus on Russia’s response to the global financial crisis, which exposed the economy’s dependence on oil, natural gas and other commodities. After years of strong growth, the fall in energy prices, decline in industrial production and retreat of foreign capital placed pressure on companies, banks and household incomes.

Reports will look at the continued importance of state-backed energy groups and the challenges facing foreign investors, including concerns about regulation, property rights, corporate governance and political intervention. At the same time, CNN will highlight efforts to diversify the economy through technology, telecommunications, retail, manufacturing and consumer services.

Moscow’s transformation will provide one measure of the changes. Luxury stores, new restaurants and major construction projects reflect the wealth created during the energy boom, while commuters, pensioners and families outside the capital often face a sharply different reality.

The coverage will also examine Russia’s growing middle class and its evolving expectations. Greater access to foreign travel, imported goods and digital communications has altered consumer habits and opened new avenues for public discussion, even as the government maintains extensive influence over traditional broadcasting.

## A culture shaped by tradition and reinvention

CNN International will devote part of the special to Russia’s cultural life, presenting a country whose global image remains closely tied to literature, classical music, ballet and monumental architecture, but whose contemporary artists are experimenting with new forms and ideas.

In Moscow and St. Petersburg, reports will visit major cultural institutions as well as smaller galleries, performance spaces, fashion studios and music venues. The aim is to show how a younger generation is drawing on Soviet history and pre-revolutionary traditions while responding to the commercialism and political debates of modern Russia.

The country’s architecture will offer another lens on its past and present. The Kremlin and Red Square stand alongside Stalin-era towers, Soviet apartment blocks, restored churches and glass-fronted commercial developments. Similar contrasts can be found in St. Petersburg, where imperial palaces and canals coexist with the pressures of tourism, development and preservation.

Food and nightlife will also feature, reflecting the expansion of Russia’s restaurant industry and the revival of regional cooking. Traditional dishes remain central to national identity, but urban chefs and entrepreneurs are increasingly reinterpreting them for a new generation of diners.

## Sports and the road to Sochi

Russia’s sporting ambitions will form another major element of the coverage. The country is investing heavily in facilities and infrastructure as it prepares to host the 2014 Winter Olympic Games in Sochi, a Black Sea resort better known domestically for beaches and subtropical summers than for snow sports.

CNN will examine the scale of the Sochi project, including the construction of mountain venues, transport links, hotels and new urban infrastructure. The preparations are being promoted as evidence that Russia can stage a complex international event and modernize an entire region.

The reports will also consider the costs and controversies associated with the development, from environmental concerns to the challenge of completing projects on schedule in difficult terrain.

Elsewhere, the network will look at Russia’s deep sporting traditions, including ice hockey, gymnastics, figure skating, tennis and football. Sport remains a powerful source of national pride, and success in international competition is closely followed by both the public and the country’s political leadership.

## Russia beyond the familiar landmarks

Travel reports will take viewers beyond the Kremlin, Red Square and St. Petersburg’s palaces to emphasize Russia’s extraordinary scale and regional diversity.

Potential destinations include the historic towns of the Golden Ring, the Volga River, Siberia and communities along the Trans-Siberian Railway. The coverage will show landscapes ranging from forests and lakes to industrial cities and remote settlements, while examining how distance and climate shape life in the world’s largest country.

The travel segments will also address the practical realities facing visitors, including transportation, accommodation and the contrast between Russia’s increasingly international cities and regions where tourism infrastructure remains limited.

By combining diplomacy with reporting on entrepreneurs, athletes, artists and ordinary families, CNN International’s special aims to provide context for Obama’s visit that extends beyond the summit table.

The U.S. president’s meetings in Moscow may produce agreements on weapons, security and bilateral cooperation. But the network’s broader portrait will focus on the country behind those negotiations: a Russia seeking modernization and international recognition while continuing to wrestle with the political structures, economic dependencies and historical legacies that define its place in the 21st century.
